Members

The people behind the science

Principal Investigator

Doyun Lee

Principal Investigator
Senior Research Fellow

Center for Memory and Glioscience, IBS

✉ leedoyun@ibs.re.kr

Doyun Lee received his PhD in Physiology from Seoul National University in 2007. He established the Doyun Lee Lab as an independent research group at the Center for Memory and Glioscience, Institute for Basic Science (IBS) in June 2015.

His research focuses on understanding the neural mechanisms underlying social cognition, with a particular emphasis on how the brain represents and processes social identity information.

Since 2020, he holds the position of Senior Research Fellow at IBS.

Education
  • Postdoc, Albert Lee lab, Janelia Research Campus / Howard Hughes Medical Institute (2008.11 – 2015.4)
  • PhD, Department of Physiology, College of Medicine, Seoul National University (2007)
  • MS, Department of Molecular Biology, Seoul National University (2000)
  • BS, Department of Molecular Biology, Seoul National University (1998)
  • Korea Science Academy 1기 (previously Busan Science High School)
Research Interests
  • Neural mechanisms of social cognition and individual recognition
  • Social motivation and autism spectrum disorder
  • Large-scale neural population coding
  • In vivo electrophysiology and calcium imaging
